heading: Services are compiled in
body:
Tachyon compiles a `<Name>Service.swift`, `.kt`, `.cs` or `.rs` file in client/services for a supported target and includes it in the host. A Rust, C#, Swift or Kotlin service may have no browser sibling. Then it also compiles to WebAssembly. The browser runs that WebAssembly, and so does the web view of any target that does not link the service: iOS and Android for Rust, every target except Windows for C#, Windows, Linux and Android for Swift, and every target except Android for Kotlin (ADR 0035, ADR 0037, ADR 0078, ADR 0082; an ADR is an architecture decision record). A Go or Java service links into no host, so it always compiles to WebAssembly and runs in the web view on every target (ADR 0045, ADR 0083). Swift and Rust use native compilation. A Swift method marked `async`, such as a `@Cached` method, runs on macOS and iOS too: the host waits for it on the main thread and keeps the main run loop turning, so work that the method sends to the main actor can finish. Kotlin uses the Android toolchain. C# uses the Windows .NET host. In all other cases, the browser runs the `.js`, `.ts` or `.dart` file next to them. Native service code reaches the platform SDK with the operating system permissions of the host process. So every service reaches every target.

A Swift or Kotlin service with `NeedsAll` can declare a field without a value, such as `let title: String`. Tachyon generates the constructor that fills it from the props of the component (ADR 0057). When a prop is missing or has the wrong type, Tachyon does not create the service, and the page gets the error code `TY_NATIVE_REQUIRED`.
